problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4x-3y,\,y(-1)=1
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(-\frac{1}{3}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(-\frac{1}{3})≈{{field-1}}
$$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=-\frac{1}{3},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=-\frac{1}{3}-(-1)=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4x-3y+(4{x}_{\text{new}}-3{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4x-3y+4{x}_{\text{new}}-3{y}_{\text{new}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-3y)-{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{3}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}}-3y)-{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{3}(4x+4{x}_{\text{new}})-{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{4}{3}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{2}{3}(x+{x}_{\text{new}})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=-1+\frac{2}{3}=-\frac{1}{3}.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{2}{3}(x+{x}_{\text{new}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-1+(-\frac{1}{3})) \\  & =-\frac{8}{9} \\  & ≈-0.89.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\,(-\frac{1}{3})≈-0.89.$
